previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: A woman with end-stage renal disease on hemodialysis, a mechanical aortic valve, and extensive cardiovascular disease was admitted for substernal chest pain during dialysis. She had elevated troponins without EKG changes, consistent with NSTEMI, and was managed initially with nitroglycerin and blood pressure control. Due to recent gastrointestinal bleeding and elevated INR, cardiac catheterization was delayed until anticoagulation was stabilized. A drug-eluting stent was placed in the mid-LAD artery on hospital day 5, after which her chest pain resolved. She was treated for volume overload with three dialysis sessions, improving pulmonary congestion. A possible pneumonia was ruled out, and antibiotics were discontinued. Her INR was maintained at a new target of 1.8–2.5 to balance clotting and bleeding risks. She was discharged home with home health services on dual anticoagulation (warfarin and clopidogrel), with aspirin to be discontinued after one month, and instructions to continue dialysis, wound care for a left heel ulcer, and outpatient follow-up.

requested to be seen by palliative care while she was here, as

===============
ACUTE ISSUES
===============
# Goals of Care: Mrs. ___ and ___ husband were seen by 
palliative care. There was a long discussion about her past 
history and wishes for her future goals of care. She reports 
that she is exhausted from her medical problems and has 
expressed that she is considering signing off from dialysis in 
the future and is interested in finding out more about hospice 
care and what they can offer her. She ultimately decided that 
she will continue dialysis until her son is able to come and 
visit. Through that time, she does not want to come to the 
hospital and would like symptom control at home. Once her son 
has visited, she reports that she will likely discontinue 
dialysis. She will be discharged on home hospice.

# NSTEMI: Patient admitted with chest pain and troponin 
elevation, consistent with Type II NSTEMI given anemia and HTN. 
In light of her current intermittent symptoms and review of her 
most recent angiogram, it is unlikely that any vessel disease 
will be amenable to angioplasty and it is best treated 
medically. To help with symptom control, we maximized medical 
therapy by adding isosorbide and ranolazine to her medications. 
She could not tolerate SL nitro because it dropped her BPs so 
she took PO dilaudid PRN pain. She also underwent blood 
transfusions while in the hospital.

# Anemia: Hb 7.9 this morning. No signs or symptoms of GI 
bleeding. She underwent several transfusions while in the 
hospital.

# Hyperkalemia: Patient reports her K often fluctuates. Her K 
was 4.8 the morning after admission (down from ___ yesterday). 
Evidence of hyperacute T waves on EKG on presentation, but K < 6 
for the rest of the hospitalization. 
=====================
CHRONIC ISSUES
=====================
# Mechanical aortic valve: Currently subtherapeutic. Given high 
risk of stroke and Hct stability, will initiate heparin drip. 
Remained on heparin gtt as brisge to coumadin until INR 
therapeutic.  

# LLE heel wound: Santyl, hydrogel, wound consult.  

# Hypertension: Will follow home regimen with labetalol 300 TID, 
holding on HD days in AM and if < 130, and amlodipine 10 mg 
daily with holding  with the addition for isosorbide.

# ESRD on HD: HD with tunneled R IJ line. S/p failed transplant 
x 2, will continue prednisone as well as calcium, nephrocaps. 
Discussed with Dr. ___ palliative care re: long-term 
goals for dialysis and management of ESRD. EPO every other week 

# Chronic CHFpEF, compensated: Continue to monitor for signs of 
volume overload after transfusion.  

# Atrial fibrillation: Paroxysmal. Currently in sinus rhythm, 
anticoagulation as above.  
 
# PVD: Stable. Continue aspirin, statin, and gabapentin.  
# HLD: Statin as above, continue gemfibrozil. Note risk of 
myopathy with gemfibrozil and statin.  
# Asthma: Stable. Will continue albuterol.
